hints: Look closely at lactide, it is a cyclic molecule with two ester groups, so think about what reaction forms esters from hydroxy acids.
Split the ring in half at the two ester links, each half has three carbons including one methyl side chain.
Ask yourself which hydroxy acid with three carbons could join in pairs and lose two water molecules to close that six-membered ring.
walkthrough:
**Spot what lactide is**

Lactide is a cyclic diester. It has two $\text{C-O-C=O}$ ester links in a six-membered ring.

That tells us it was made by esterification, which needs a carboxylic acid group and an alcohol group with loss of water.

**Work backwards by hydrolysis**

Imagine adding two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules across the two ester bonds to open the ring.

$$\text{lactide} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2 \times \text{hydroxy acid monomer}$$

So lactide must come from two identical hydroxy acid molecules joining together.

**Identify the monomer unit**

Look at one half of the ring. Each half contains $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH-COO}$ joined through oxygen.

That fragment comes from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$, which is 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid). Two molecules condense on heating with acid catalyst to give lactide plus water:
$$2\,\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH} \rightarrow \text{lactide} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Hydroxyethanoic acid is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COOH}$. Two molecules would condense to give glycolide, a ring with no methyl groups. Lactide clearly has two methyl groups, so this monomer is too small.
options.B: 2-hydroxybutanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)COOH}$. Its dimer would have two ethyl side chains ($\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) on the ring, not the two methyl groups ($\text{CH}_3$) seen in lactide.
options.C: 2-hydroxypropanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$. Two molecules undergo intermolecular esterification on heating with acid catalyst, losing two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to form the six-membered cyclic diester with two methyl groups, which is exactly lactide.
options.D: 3-hydroxypropanoic acid is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. The OH is on carbon 3, so it would form a different sized ring and would have no methyl branches. It cannot give the methyl-substituted six-membered ring shown.
